Onboarding/Intro/SubHeading: Let's get you setup and started!
Onboarding/HowItWorks/NeedsYouBody: Opens to a tab that groups PRs by why they need you: needs work, ready to merge, or blocked on you.
Onboarding/HowItWorks/MergeBody: Approved, conflict-free and CI green? A Merge button appears on the card. One click and it's merged.
Onboarding/HowItWorks/UrgencyDotBody: Red: your PR needs work. Orange: someone is blocked on you. Green: ready to merge. Toggle it in settings.
Onboarding/HowItWorks/SnoozeHideBody: Hover a PR to snooze or hide it. A snoozed PR comes back on its own as soon as it gets an update.
Onboarding/HowItWorks/NotificationsBody: One banner per PR, only on a change: review requested, changes requested, CI failed, conflicts or ready to merge.
Onboarding/HowItWorks/StatusBody: One clear status badge per card (approved, draft, changes requested or conflicts) plus the CI status.
Onboarding/HowItWorks/CompactBody: Switch to a compact view to fit more PRs on screen, perfect when you're juggling many at once
Onboarding/LaunchAtLogin/Body: To get the best out of GitBar, we recommend to start GitBar at start up of your device.
Onboarding/Notifications/ConfirmBody: Accept the permissions from Apple in the top right corner (see image for reference) to start receiving notifications.
Onboarding/Notifications/Body: By allowing notifications from GitBar you will get a banner when your review is requested, changes are requested, CI fails, conflicts appear, or your PR becomes ready to merge.
Onboarding/Issues/Body: GitHub issues will now appear in GitBar. Issues you created, or made on repos you own or collaborate on. You can turn this feature off in settings.
Onboarding/ReadyToGo/Body: Open GitBar through the menu bar icon
Settings/PullRequests/HideDrafts: Hide PRs that have a draft status
Settings/PullRequests/CompactCards: Compact PR cards (one line per PR)
Auth/GitHub/Cancelled: Something went wrong during the authentication process
Issues/Fallback/Disabled/Body: Enable issues in settings to see your GitHub issues here. You will see issues you created, are made on repos you own or collaborate on.
Issues/Fallback/NoGitHub/Body: Issues are currently only supported for GitHub. Add a GitHub account to see your issues. You will see issues you created, are made on repos you own or collaborate on.
Issues/Fallback/Empty/Body: You're all caught up! Your GitHub issues will appear here when you have open issues.
Settings/Issues/HideAfter: Hide Issues after 2 months of inactivity
Settings/Issues/Description:
Issues are currently only supported for GitHub.
It will collect issues you created, are made on repos you own or collaborate on.
